At Danaher, our work saves lives. And each of us plays a part. Fueled by our culture of continuous improvement, we turn ideas into impact – innovating at the speed of life.
Our 63,000+ associates work across the globe at more than 15 unique businesses within life sciences, diagnostics, and biotechnology.
Are you ready to accelerate your potential and make a real difference? At Danaher, you can build an incredible career at a leading science and technology company, where we’re committed to hiring and developing from within. You’ll thrive in a culture of belonging where you and your unique viewpoint matter.
Learn about the Danaher Business System which makes everything possible.
The Data Analyst keeps Danaher's workforce record accurate, secure, and audit-ready, the trusted associate data every HR service depends on and the foundation every automation and agent runs on. This is one broad role deployed across Quality & Audit, SOX & Compliance, and Integrations against the funnel of priorities.
You deliver AI-ready data and eliminate recurring defects at the source, partnering with the Product Owner and Business Analyst to fix the process, not just the record.
This position reports to the Senior Director, HR Technology and is part of the HR Technology team and will be fully remote.
## In this role, you will have the opportunity to:
• Keep the workforce record trusted, measured by data accuracy, audit findings avoided, and integration reliability, not tasks run.
• Deliver AI-ready data: structure, validate, and govern the associate record so automation and agents can operate safely on it.
• Eliminate recurring data defects at the source: partner with the Product Owner and BA to fix the process, not just correct the record.
• Quality & Audit: run data-quality controls, audits, security reviews, mass loads, and corrections on the associate master record.
• SOX & Compliance: analyze HR data against regulatory, privacy, and SOX controls, and support testing, monitoring, and audit-ready evidence.
• Integrations: validate outbound extracts and Workday integrations, reconcile, troubleshoot, and monitor downstream data flows.
## The essential requirements of the job include:
• Bachelor’s degree in computer science, Information Systems, or equivalent, and 5+ years in HR data operations, integrations, or analytics.
• Hands-on Workday integrations and outbound extracts with data validation, troubleshooting, and reconciliation.
• Strong HR data concepts, data-quality controls, and governance; demonstrated SOX/GDPR discipline through testing and audit-ready controls.
• A bias for fixing the process, not just the record.
• Workday Report Writer/Prism, calculated fields, and EIB/Studio exposure a plus.
It would be a plus if you also possess previous experience in:
• Leading global data governance or master data management initiatives in a complex, multi-business environment.
Join our winning team today. Together, we’ll accelerate the real-life impact of tomorrow’s science and technology. We partner with customers across the globe to help them solve their most complex challenges, architecting solutions that bring the power of science to life.

## Job Description: Imagery Analyst – AI/ML Training Data
Role Type: Contractor – Part-Time or Full-Time
Location: Remote
Eligibility: U.S. Citizenship and Active DoD Common Access Card (CAC) Required
## About the Role
We are seeking detail-oriented Imagery Analysts to contribute to a high-impact AI/ML training project focused on drone and maritime sensor imagery.
In this role, you will apply your imagery analysis and annotation expertise to review AI-generated labels, identify objects, and improve the accuracy of training datasets. Your contributions will help enhance how AI systems interpret and analyze real-world imagery.
No prior AI experience is required. Your subject-matter expertise and attention to detail are what matter.
Important Eligibility Requirements: This project supports a U.S. Navy contract and requires applicants to be U.S. citizens with an active DoD Common Access Card (CAC). Candidates who do not meet these requirements are not eligible for this specific project. However, other annotation opportunities may be available without these restrictions.
## Key Responsibilities
• Review and refine machine-generated bounding boxes to ensure accuracy in still imagery captured by drone and maritime sensors.
• Identify and annotate objects that have been missed by AI models.
• Label imagery consistently while following established annotation guidelines.
• Submit completed annotated images within a secure U.S. Navy project environment.
• Maintain consistent and reliable productivity, meeting project quality and submission requirements.
• Transition to video-frame annotation as the project expands.
• Document and communicate ambiguous cases, annotation challenges, and guideline-related questions clearly.
## Preferred Qualifications
• U.S. citizenship and an active DoD Common Access Card (CAC), or eligibility and willingness to participate in the CAC sponsorship process, subject to project requirements.
• Strong attention to detail and consistency when performing repetitive, accuracy-critical tasks.
• Experience with data labeling, bounding box annotation, or similar data preparation activities.
• Familiarity with aerial, maritime, or sensor-based imagery, particularly daylight and thermal imagery.
• Experience working in high-volume, quality-controlled annotation environments. Robotics or autonomous systems data-labeling experience is an advantage.
• Comfort using specialized annotation software and willingness to learn new tools.
• Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to report issues and clarify labeling requirements.

## Job Description: Computational Life Scientist – AI Training & Model Evaluation
Role Type: Contractor
Location: Global (Fully Remote)
Time Commitment: 15+ hours per week
Schedule: Flexible
## About the Role
We are seeking experienced Computational Life Scientists with prior professional AI-training or model-evaluation experience to contribute to a project focused on improving advanced AI systems.
You will apply your scientific expertise and programming skills to develop challenging technical tasks, evaluate AI-generated code and analyses, identify errors, and establish objective standards for accurate solutions. This opportunity is intended for professionals with substantive experience in AI training involving life sciences or biomedical content.
## Key Responsibilities
• Create realistic computational life-science tasks that challenge advanced AI models.
• Develop clear task instructions, reproducible environments, reference solutions, and evaluation criteria.
• Evaluate AI-generated code, analyses, models, experiments, and technical deliverables.
• Identify invalid biological assumptions, methodological errors, data leakage, statistical issues, and reproducibility failures.
• Assess the scientific accuracy, reliability, and completeness of model-generated outputs.
• Establish objective standards for evaluating computational and scientific solutions.
## Required Qualifications
• Prior paid experience training, evaluating, benchmarking, or improving AI systems on scientific or technical tasks.
• Strong practical proficiency in Python.
• Deep expertise in at least one relevant life-science specialization.
• Hands-on experience using computational methods for modeling, simulation, bioinformatics, biomedical analysis, statistics, or reproducible research.
## Relevant Specializations
• Biology
• Computational Biology
• Bioinformatics
• Medicine and Health
• Biomedical Science
• Neuroscience
• Genomics
• Ecology and Evolution
## Public Proof of Technical Expertise
Strong applicants should be able to demonstrate their expertise through evidence such as:
• Peer-reviewed publications or preprints involving computational methods.
• Public research code or bioinformatics pipelines.
• Google Scholar, ORCID, or equivalent research profiles.
• PhysioNet or other biomedical competition results.
• Open-source scientific software contributions.
• Public datasets, models, notebooks, or technical projects.
## Preferred Qualifications
• Experience creating AI-training tasks, reference answers, evaluation rubrics, graders, or benchmark problems.
• Experience reviewing technical submissions from other AI trainers.

• Previous experience with long-horizon or agentic AI evaluations.

Application Submission: Submit your application along with details of your AI-training experience, life-science specialization, and public technical evidence.
AI Interview: Complete an AI interview that includes technical and integrity checks.
Hiring Manager Review: The team evaluates your profile and interview performance.
Onboarding: Selected candidates complete project onboarding and begin their first assigned task.
## Compensation
Compensation is output-based, with payment for tasks that meet project specifications and quality requirements. Task availability and completion time may vary.

Job Title:
Vulnerability Management Engineer (AI Automation)
About Trellix
Trellix is a global cybersecurity leader helping organizations build cyber resilience for the AI era. Combining AI-native security, operational threat intelligence, and automated detection and response, Trellix provides defense-grade protection at machine speed across on-premises, air-gapped, operational technology, hybrid, and cloud environments. Trellix helps customers anticipate threats, scale effective security operations, maintain business continuity, and adapt their security posture for the modern threat landscape. Working with a broad partner ecosystem and global intelligence collaborators, Trellix helps strengthen the collective defense against cybercriminals and state-sponsored attacks. At Trellix, we empower professionals at all career stages to expand their technical expertise, lead strategic initiatives, and make a tangible global impact. Whether you are an industry pioneer or an emerging specialist, Trellix provides the tools and opportunities to enhance and expand your skill set. Join our mission to scale AI-driven cyber defense alongside an AI-accelerated threat landscape, and help build a safer, more resilient future. More at .
Role Overview:
We are looking for strategic, hands-on Security Engineer to drive end-to-end vulnerability management, governance, and risk-based prioritization across hybrid, cloud, and containerized environments in alignment with NIST SSDF, EU CRA, and IEC standards. The role focuses on engineering autonomous AI agents to automate asset discovery, finding validation, exploitability analysis, ticket orchestration, and zero-day response. Candidates will lead cross-functional remediation with IT and DevOps teams, streamline exception workflows, and deliver executive-level risk reporting and metrics.
## About Role:
• Direct continuous asset discovery, vulnerability assessment, remediation verification, and executive reporting across hybrid cloud, container, and application ecosystems.
• Contextualize vulnerability severity (CVSS) using real-world threat intelligence (EPSS, CISA KEV) and business criticality. Spearhead rapid response protocols for critical zero-day vulnerabilities, implementing interim compensating controls and formal risk-acceptance workflows as required.
• Architect and deploy autonomous AI agents to automate asset discovery, CMDB reconciliation, false-positive elimination, exploitability analysis, intelligent ticket routing, SLA breach escalations, and executive reporting.
• Establish and enforce program governance, remediation SLAs, and exception management frameworks aligned with NIST SSDF, EU CRA, and IEC standards.
• Define, track, and present key performance indicators (scan coverage, MTTR, SLA adherence, and vulnerability aging) to senior leadership. Partner with and mentor IT Operations, DevOps, and Software Engineering teams to accelerate remediation and embed security-by-design practices.
## About You:
• 5+ years in Information Security with a strong focus on Vulnerability Management, Application Security, or Cloud Security.
• Extensive hands-on expertise with industry-leading VM, CNAPP, and AppSec solutions—including Tenable, Wiz, Qualys, CrowdStrike, or Snyk—with proven ability to programmatically orchestrate scans, ingest telemetry, and validate remediation.
• Demonstrated experience designing and deploying autonomous AI agents and multi-step LLM workflows using frameworks such as LangChain, LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen, or OpenAI/Anthropic SDKs to automate discovery, reconciliation, and remediation pipelines.
• Proficiency in leveraging LLMs and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) architectures to correlate vulnerability data with source code repositories, asset metadata, and exploit intelligence to filter false positives and determine real-world exploitability.
• Strong proficiency in Python for developing production-grade security automation, custom integrations, and consuming or building REST and GraphQL APIs.
• Proven experience integrating security scanners with SOAR platforms, enterprise ticketing systems (Jira, ServiceNow), CMDBs, and collaboration platforms (Slack, Microsoft Teams) for automated ticket creation, routing, reminders, and SLA escalations.
• Deep command of CVSS, EPSS, and CISA KEV methodologies, with experience enriching vulnerability telemetry using threat feeds and business impact assessments.
• Comprehensive understanding of cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, GCP), hybrid enterprise networks, container orchestration (Docker, Kubernetes), and CI/CD pipelines.
• Working knowledge of NIST SSDF, EU CRA, and IEC regulatory frameworks, paired with the ability to build automated executive dashboards tracking MTTR, scan coverage, and SLA compliance.

title: Software Engineer
description:
## About Us
Zepto is building the beating heart of Australia's real-time, account-to-account payments revolution.
It's a good moment to be doing this work. Card surcharging rules have changed, Payday Super is live, and many businesses are taking a serious look at account-to-account payments for the first time. A lot of that shift lands on our platform, and we're looking for action-oriented engineers to help build category-defining infrastructure.
Payments is a domain where the details matter. When someone's wages or a business's cash flow moves through our platform, it has to arrive correctly, every time, in seconds. Meeting that bar in a regulated industry makes for interesting engineering problems. As a Software Engineer you'll own real pieces of how we solve them, working alongside senior engineers who'll help you grow your scope quickly.
We're a remote-first team that works closely together. Engineers here are trusted to make decisions, encouraged to share their thinking, and supported to grow. That culture is part of why we've been named FinTech Organisation of the Year at the Finnies twice.
## What You'll Do
• Build and maintain features on our high-volume, real-time payment APIs, shipping clean, tested, observable code into a mission-critical, regulated environment.
• Work in a cross-functional team, contributing to technical designs and RFCs and turning them into well-scoped, shippable work.
• Review your peers' code and pair regularly, learning from senior engineers and sharing what you know.
• Collaborate with Platform, Security and Incident Management teams, and join our shared on-call rotation once you're up to speed.
## What You'll Bring
• Solid backend foundations: Commercial experience in a backend language and API development. We work in Ruby and Go. Ruby experience is a plus, but strong fundamentals and a willingness to learn matter more to us than your current language.
• Good engineering practices: Experience with test-driven development, code review and continuous delivery. Exposure to public cloud (preferably AWS) or event-driven systems is a plus.
• Ownership: You take a piece of work from inception to production and make sure it works once it's there.
• AI adoption: AI is changing how engineering works, and you're evolving with it. You use tools like Claude Code or Cursor in your day-to-day delivery and stay curious as capabilities improve, while reviewing generated code as carefully as your own and respecting data security boundaries.
• Clear, open communication: You share work in progress early, ask good questions, and raise risks when you see them. You ask for help early when you're stuck.
• Front-end experience (React, TypeScript) is a bonus: Plenty of our work spans the stack, from the APIs that move money to the merchant-facing UIs built on them, so engineers who can follow their work through to the UI add real value.
## Your First 6 Months
• Week 1: You'll be paired with an onboarding buddy to get familiar with our domains, understand the business context across teams, and ship your first changes to production.
• Month 1: You're delivering stories within your team's domain and reviewing code with growing context. You understand how merchants and internal staff use the Zepto platform, and you're building relationships across product, engineering and the wider business. You've probably spotted something we could do better, whether that's a clunky endpoint, a confusing error message or a gap in our docs, and either fixed it or raised it with the team.
• Month 6: You're delivering features end to end with growing independence: working through requirements with product, contributing to the design, and seeing your work land in production. You've contributed to an RFC, you're part of the on-call rotation, and you're confident supporting the systems your team owns.
## Why Zepto?
Headquartered in beautiful Byron Bay, Zepto has an inspiring founder story and is a customer-focused, culture-first organisation. You'll be joining a team that champions curiosity and a pioneering perspective, and thrives in a fast-moving sector.
Just some of Zepto's commitments to our people include:
• Join a Talented Team: Work with world-class talent and leaders who support career growth
• Flexible Work: A remote-first work culture, with the opportunity to work anywhere in Australia. You'll also get access to premium co-working spaces and a Byron, Sydney & Melbourne Hub
• Paid Parental Leave: 12 weeks Paid Parental Leave for primary caregivers and 4 weeks for secondary caregivers
• Wellbeing Focus: Access to Zepto's Wellbeing Menu, which includes 3 x paid Wellbeing Days per year and access to an Employee Assistance Program
• Annual Learning Budget: An individual learning budget, and 4 x paid Growth & Impact Days annually to focus on professional development
• Remote-Work Support: A $500 Remote Work Budget to set up your home office upon commencement, and $300 annually from your 2nd Zeptoversary

## WHAT YOU'LL GET IN RETURN
The freedom, trust, and tools to do what you love and make an impact in a purpose-driven company, committed to doing genuine good in the digital world
Enjoy a high degree of flexibility with tailored working hours, choice of work location, and benefits that support your lifestyle, health, and family needs
Join a secure, future-focused role in a dynamic scale-up positioned to make a major impact in the rapidly expanding Security & Compliance market
Grow along expert or leadership paths with support from employee accelerator programs, bi-annual feedback cycles, and a personal training budget

You think in problems, solutions and how to implement them properly to deliver value to customers, not tickets that should to be done.

title: Software Engineer (All Levels), United Kingdom
description:
We are open to hiring at multiple levels for this role, depending on experience, impact, and demonstrated ownership. While this role is level-agnostic, it is best suited for engineers with experience owning production systems and working in highly ambiguous problem spaces.

Software Engineer

About the company: 

In the coming decades, demand for critical minerals such as copper, lithium, and cobalt will continue to grow. These minerals are needed to build electric infrastructure, vehicles, data centers, and electronics. However, the mining industry is making 10x fewer discoveries per dollar spent on exploration compared to 30 years ago because the easy-to-find, near surface deposits have largely been discovered.

KoBold was founded to be the first AI native mineral exploration, mine development, and technology development company. Our goal is to turn mineral exploration into a repeatable science to discover the minerals the world needs—by integrating artificial intelligence, human intelligence, and new technology. Our multidisciplinary teams of data scientists, engineers, and geologists work together to build data systems, design new sensors, and establish industry-leading workflows to develop and test subsurface predictions on our exploration projects.

Our first discovery, Mingomba, is a high-grade copper deposit in Zambia, found after spending materially less than industry average. We are developing Mingomba with the same technical rigor that we apply to exploration. The Mingomba team brings together mine and processing engineers, geologists, data scientists, software engineers, and community, health & safety, construction, and operations specialists. By combining industry knowledge and cutting edge technology, we are developing Mingomba into a world class project that has safer and more predictable outcomes for ourselves, partners, and communities. It is expected to create thousands of good jobs for generations.

KoBold runs exploration programs in eight countries, all with the potential for another discovery.

KoBold is privately held; investors include institutional asset managers T. Rowe Price and Canada Pension Plan Investments; technology venture capitalists Andreessen Horowitz, Breakthrough Energy Ventures, BOND Capital, Durable Capital, StepStone, and Standard Investments; and strategic natural resources companies BHP and Mitsubishi.

We are hiring Software Engineers to accelerate our mission.

 

About The Role:

At KoBold, software engineers have the unique opportunity to embed directly with their users and learn the ins and outs of mineral exploration and geology while developing state of the art technology solutions. Unlike traditional software engineering roles, we don’t simply ship code and passively wait for feedback about its utility: our userbase includes our colleagues… and ourselves! While there are real technical challenges in making mineral exploration data broadly searchable and accessible to both humans and machines, we believe that solving these technical challenges cannot be done without “getting our hands dirty” – sometimes literally! – by embedding directly with the exploration teams and even occasionally (~once a year) joining our colleagues in the field, be it in Zambia, Canada, or Arizona, to experience the impact of our software in real time.

 

As a Software Engineer on the Data Systems Engineering team at KoBold, your main role will be to enable systematic exploration and materially improve exploration success rates by making mineral exploration data broadly accessible to humans and machines.  Past projects have included SIP (the Structured Ingest Pipeline), DataKit generation (producing curated sets of data on demand), and RAG (Retrieval Augmentation Generation, utilizing natural language processing on unstructured data). Our tech stack is primarily python and includes Django, React, AWS, and additional technologies like Retool and Prefect. 

 

Your work will empower KoBold to unlock invaluable insights and streamline intricate scientific processes. Collaborating with our exceptional team of data scientists, geologists, and other software engineers, you will have the opportunity to tackle complex problems head-on and collectively pave the way for the discoveries of vital energy transition metals like lithium, copper, nickel, and cobalt. Together we can shape the future of mineral exploration and contribute to building a sustainable world.

 

This role be responsible for:

  • Deep engagement with exploration geologists and data scientists, continual learning about mineral exploration, and tailoring technology development to the needs of exploration project scientists
  • Building data pipelines and tooling for deriving advanced human and machine insights from exploration data, often leading a small group of software engineers to successful delivery
  • Developing expertise in KoBold’s Data Systems and deeply understanding how they impact exploration
  • End-to-end ownership of projects from design to implementation and testing to continued engagement with colleagues on exploration teams using your solutions
  • Responding well to design and code feedback, also providing feedback to teammates 
  • Operationally managing the team’s services and assisting scientific colleagues with our tooling

 

Qualifications

  • 4+ years of software engineering experience, ideally building production cloud data systems
  • Proficiency with Python
  • Ability to write production-quality code that is correct, readable, well-tested, scalable and extensible
  • Skilled in large-scale system design
  • A track record of taking ownership from definition of the problem and delivering projects with demonstrated impact in an iterative manner
  • Intellectual curiosity and eagerness to learn about all aspects of mineral exploration, particularly in the geology domain. Enjoys constantly learning such that you are driving insights through using our tools in exploration and willing to work directly with geologists in the field.
  • Ability to explain technical problems to and collaborate on solutions with domain experts who are not software developers. A strong communicator who enjoys working with colleagues across the company.
  • Excitement about joining a fast-growing early-stage company, comfort with a dynamic work environment, and eagerness to take on an evolving range of responsibilities.
  • Keen not just to build cool technology, but to figure out what technical product to build to best achieve the business objectives of the company.

Nice to Haves 

  • Experience with modern frontend frameworks such as React
  • Experience with geospatial data and building map-based experiences

title: CENTRALE LYON - Post-doctoral researcher (12 months) Mathematics of energy-efficient AI: diffusion models on emerging hardware
description:
The question
Generating one image with a diffusion model means evaluating a large neural network tens to hundreds of times. That repetition is where the energy goes, and it is part of why data-centre demand is now visible at grid scale: the Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory puts US data-centre electricity use at 176 TWh in 2023, 4.4 % of national consumption, a figure that more than doubled since 2017 largely because of AI servers, and projects 325–580 TWh by 2028. Emerging hardware attacks exactly this primitive: analog in-memory computing, silicon photonics, ferroelectric devices and stochastic computing perform the underlying matrix–vector products at lower energy than digital CMOS, under conditions on scale and precision, but return a perturbed result. The usual objection is that nobody can say in advance how much perturbation a model tolerates. In EMMA, this opportunity is pursued through a PCM-based photonic matrix–vector engine as the primary demonstrator, complemented where appropriate by FeFET-based analog computing, so that device-level non-idealities are treated as explicit design parameters rather than as after-the-fact implementation losses. Diffusion models are an unusual case in which that question has a mathematical answer: their convergence theory bounds the discrepancy between the generated and target distributions by three terms, of which only one, the L 2 error of the learned score, depends on the hardware. That side is now in good shape: for stochastic samplers, bounds linear in the dimension under minimal assumptions on the data; for deterministic samplers, a matching theory under regularity. What is missing is the bridge. The theory is parameterised by a score error, the hardware literature by conductance noise, effective number of bits and photons per multiply–accumulate; nobody has written the map between them, in either direction. The quantisation literature for diffusion models reports image-quality scores; the induced L 2 score error, in the form the convergence theory needs, is directly measurable and goes unreported. One open sub-question sets the direction: the distinction between an error redrawn at each evaluation, as in stochastic computing, and an error frozen at write time, as in deterministic quantisation, has been settled in one setting only, and not the one hardware lives in; carrying it over is what this position exists to do. The work is judged on one concrete outcome. For at least one architecture, we want to show that theenergy gain from moving the score evaluation off digital CMOS is real, measured where it survives integration and not extrapolated from a single tile, and that it is paid for by a loss in sample quality that is small and, above all, tunable: a knob the designer sets, whose position the theory predicts rather than discovers afterwards.
What you will do
The work is organised in four packages, summarised below; the full research programme is available from the supervisors on request.
1. Make the score error measurable, starting from Gaussian targets where the whole error decomposition is closed-form. You will report the induced score error for a given perturbation of the network’s arithmetic, the number the theory needs and the quantisation literature does not report.
2. Map device physics onto the theory. Propagate the published error models for the technologies INL works on through the score network into an explicit score-error budget, separating what is proved from what is measured.
3. Extend the guarantees. Existing bounds assume a deterministic oracle, or a benign randomised one; extend them to error that is part frozen at write time and part redrawn at each call, and settle, on the way, which process the score error should be controlled along.
4. Co-design with INL, and deliver the proof of concept. Turn the score-error budget into an energy– accuracy frontier for INL’s PCM-based photonic matrix–vector engine, using device-calibrated circuitlevel models; a FeFET-based analog alternative may be considered where appropriate. Jointly vary sampler steps, stochastic bitstream length and effective precision to identify an operating point predicted to yield a real energy advantage over digital CMOS at a small, tunable loss in sample quality. The result is a frontier predicted from mathematical and hardware models, then verified against calibrated measurements.
A clear negative answer is more useful to us than a vague positive one: a negative result on point 3 leaves points 1 and 2 intact and turns point 4 from a prediction into a measurement.
Who we are looking for Required
• A PhD in applied mathematics, statistics, machine learning, electronic engineering, computer science or a closely related field, obtained (or with the defence scheduled) before the start of the contract.
• A strong foundation in probability and stochastic analysis, numerical analysis, optimisation, or machine learning: SDEs, Girsanov’s theorem, time reversal of diffusions, with the ability to apply it rigorously to diffusion or other generative models.
• Familiarity with the convergence theory of sampling algorithms, or the demonstrated capacity to acquire it quickly, for example through Langevin/MCMC analysis, optimal transport or concentration of measure.
• Solid scientific computing (PyTorch or JAX), and the habit of writing code others can run. Ability and motivation to work across mathematical modelling and hardware-aware AI.
• Working English; French is not required.
Valued, not required
Prior work on diffusion or score-based generative models; numerical analysis of finite-precision arithmetic. Familiarity with hardware-aware machine learning, approximate or stochastic computing, analogue in-memory computing, device modelling, circuit simulation, photonics, ferroelectric devices, or energy modelling. Experience linking model accuracy or robustness to implementation non-idealities, such as quantisation, noise, drift, variability, finite precision, or correlated errors. Evidence of interdisciplinary research, for example work at the interface of mathematics, machine learning, devices, circuits, architectures, or electronic-design automation. No hardware experience is expected or needed to apply.
What matters most
We are seeking a researcher who wants to explore how to turn physical constraints into mathematical and architectural design parameters. The project does not require prior laboratory hardware experience: INL provides device expertise, measured characteristics and modelling infrastructure. However, the successful candidate must be prepared to engage critically with non-ideal analog, photonic and ferroelectric accelerators, and to work with both supervisors to connect device-level error mechanisms, score-error guarantees and the energy–quality trade-off of diffusion-model inference. Candidates with a primarily mathematical background and strong curiosity for hardware are welcome, as are candidates from AIhardware, device-modeling, circuit, architecture or EDA backgrounds who have the stochastic-analysis maturity needed to develop the theory. The decisive criterion is the ability to make the mathematics and hardware inform one another, producing predictions that are quantitative, testable and relevant to an energy-efficient accelerator demonstrator.
What we offer
• A real double supervision, with weekly meetings that alternate between ICJ and INL. The two laboratories are on the same campus, five minutes apart on foot.
• A question publishable on both sides: mathematics journals for the theory, design and hardware venues for the co-design.
• Involvement in INL’s design–technology co-optimisation work through the PEPR Électronique CHOOSE project, and contact with the group’s ferroelectric and photonic device work (FVLLMONTI, Ferro4EdgeAI).
• Support for conference travel and open-access publication, funded by the two host laboratories, and the career-development measures the establishment provides for post-doctoral researchers.
• Practical help for international recruits through Espace ULYS, the EURAXESS service centre for Université de Lyon: visas, housing, health cover, banking, schooling.
Conditions
Twelve-month fixed-term contract under French public law, full time (1 607 h annual reference), 25 working days of annual leave plus the RTT days of the establishment’s scheme. Affiliation to the régime général for health and to IRCANTEC for supplementary pension; employer contribution to complementary health cover under the scheme in force at the establishment; 75 % reimbursement of publictransport season tickets, up to the statutory ceiling. The exact number of RTT days is set by the establishment.
